Create a polished, working CHIP-8 emulator and visual debugger in one self-contained file: chip8_anthropic-claude-haiku-5-5_01.html.

Use inline HTML, CSS and JavaScript only: no libraries, CDNs, external assets, backend or network requests. It must work offline via file://. Every control must work and every displayed value must reflect real emulator state.

1. EMULATOR CORE

Implement 4096 writable memory bytes, the standard 80-byte font at 0x050, ROM loading at 0x200, sixteen 8-bit registers V0-VF, 16-bit I and PC, a 16-entry return stack, DT/ST timers, a 64x32 framebuffer and 16-key input. Support self-modifying code.

Implement all 34 executable base CHIP-8 patterns:
00E0, 00EE, 1NNN, 2NNN, 3XNN, 4XNN, 5XY0, 6XNN, 7XNN,
8XY0, 8XY1, 8XY2, 8XY3, 8XY4, 8XY5, 8XY6, 8XY7, 8XYE,
9XY0, ANNN, BNNN, CXNN, DXYN, EX9E, EXA1, FX07, FX0A,
FX15, FX18, FX1E, FX29, FX33, FX55, FX65.

Recognize legacy SYS 0NNN, often counted as instruction 35; report it as unsupported after decoding 00E0/00EE. Do not emulate native COSMAC 1802 routines or add partial SUPER-CHIP/XO-CHIP support.

Decode exact patterns: 5XY1 and 9XY1 are invalid. Handle carry, no-borrow including equality, shifted-out bits, BCD and inclusive V0-VX transfers correctly. Capture operands before writes; write arithmetic/shift results before VF. Test X=F, Y=F and X=Y. Capture sprite coordinates before clearing VF. 7XNN does not separately modify VF.

Use these explicit default compatibility settings:
- Shifts use VX; FX55/65 preserve I; BNNN uses NNN+V0.
- Logic operations do not separately reset VF.
- Drawing starts at coordinates modulo 64/32, then clips at right/bottom edges.
- FX1E wraps I to 16 bits and leaves VF unchanged.
- FX29 uses 0x050 + 5*(VX & 0x0F).
- FX0A waits for a fresh keydown, ignoring previously held keys and repeats.
- DXY0 draws nothing and sets VF=0; no vertical-blank drawing wait.

- Compatibility settings (switchable while paused, default values): shiftSource='VX' (alternative 'VY'); loadStoreIncrement=false (alternative: I = I+X+1 after FX55/FX65 when true); logicResetVF=false (alternative: 8XY1/2/3 set VF=0 when true); spriteWrap=false (alternative: wrap pixels at edges when true; start coordinates always modulo 64/32); BNNN uses NNN+V0.
- Faults: unknown opcode, unsupported 0NNN, invalid fetch (PC odd is allowed but fetch must be within 0..4094), out-of-bounds memory access, stack overflow/underflow. Faults pause execution, silence audio, and record faulting address, opcode, and explanation. No silent address wrap.
- Timers: tick(), decrements DT and ST by 1 at 60Hz when called by the UI; not affected by pause; DT/ST still decrement during FX0A waits.
- Trace: ring buffer of last 200 completed instructions: sequence, previous PC, opcode, mnemonic, resulting PC, register changes, memory writes, stack-depth change. Log FX0A once when completed.
- Memory write tracking per step (includes unchanged-value writes) for hex dump highlighting.
- Breakpoints: Set of addresses; stop BEFORE executing an instruction at a breakpoint; resuming bypasses the current breakpoint once; single step executes through it without removing it.
- Reset: restores original ROM and full machine state while keeping UI preferences and valid breakpoints; must not duplicate execution loops.

UI (vanilla DOM, dark graphite theme with cyan and amber accents, system UI fonts, monospace data, responsive desktop/mobile layout, visible focus rings):
- Top bar: ROM controls (Load ROM file picker, Load Demo button, drag-and-drop onto the page), filename, size, address range (0x200-...), status badge: PAUSED / RUNNING / WAITING / BREAKPOINT / FAULT.
- Transport: Run, Pause, Single Step, Reset. Instructions-per-second slider 60-6000 plus numeric input, default 600; CPU execution driven by elapsed-time accumulator via requestAnimationFrame, not per frame instruction count. Timers at 60Hz via separate accumulator.

- Audio: Web Audio oscillator beep, only while ST>0 and running; initialized on first user gesture (Run button); mute toggle, volume slider; activity indicator; silence on pause/fault/reset.
- Registers panel: V0-VF hex and decimal, highlight changes after steps, VF distinct styling; editable while paused with validation (0-255 for V, 0-0xFFF for I, even-or-any valid PC within 0..4095, timers 0-255); I, PC, SP, DT, ST, instruction count, next opcode.
- Stack panel: all 16 entries, active slots, top marker, return addresses; click an address to navigate disassembly there.
- Disassembly panel: address, raw bytes (actual byte pair at PC even at odd addresses), mnemonic, operands, brief explanation; PC marked NEXT, last executed marked separately; Follow PC toggle; go-to-address input; breakpoint gutter click toggles breakpoints; invalid instructions marked; note that linear disassembly can interpret sprite data as code and does not recover source. Shares decode() with the core.
- Memory panel: hex dump of 4096 bytes, 16 per row, ASCII column, go-to-address, jump to PC and I, distinct markers for PC, I, font, ROM; highlight memory writes from latest step; validated byte editing when paused.
- Sprite preview: 8 pixels wide, from I or selected address, height 1-15, shows byte values; safe end-of-memory handling.
- Breakpoint list with add/remove.
- Trace panel: last 200 entries, clear, follow-latest toggle.
- Keypad: 4x4 virtual keypad with mapping 1 2 3 C -> 1 2 3 4; 4 5 6 D -> Q W E R; 7 8 9 E -> A S D F; A 0 B F -> Z X C V, showing both virtual and physical labels. KeyboardEvent.code based (Digit1, Digit2, Digit3, Digit4, KeyQ, KeyW, KeyE, KeyR, KeyA, KeyS, KeyD, KeyF, KeyZ, KeyX, KeyC, KeyV). Keydown/keyup, simultaneous keys, pointer events with pointer capture and pointercancel handling, touch-action none on keys. Clear all held keys on window blur. Do not intercept keys when focus is in input/textarea/select/contentEditable.
- Demo ROM: an original CHIP-8 program embedded as a byte array with annotated assembly comments, implementing: sprite movement with keys 2/4/6/8 (visible physical bindings shown), XOR erase/redraw, DT-paced movement, a real CALL/RET drawing subroutine, key-triggered ST beep, an FX0A start interaction, and movement near edges demonstrating clipping. Everything must be executed through CHIP-8 instructions; JS must not animate the demo or fabricate values.
- Pausing on document visibilitychange hidden (discard background elapsed time). Starts with demo loaded and paused.
- Self-tests button "Run Self-tests": creates isolated Chip8Core instances, runs checks on arithmetic/flags edge cases (X=F, Y=F, X=Y), shifts, skips, CALL/RET, BCD, register transfers, compatibility switches, XOR collision, FX0A wait, timer ticks, invalid operations, reset after self-modification, with a deterministic PRNG for CXNN. Show expected vs observed and pass/fail totals, without changing the user's session.
- Debugger refresh throttled while running; full refresh immediately after pause, step, edits. Avoid unbounded loops.

Output must be complete valid HTML with no placeholders, no TODO comments, and no omitted code."}
